Chief ACK + LANDED: the externalMass fix 59f8fd0 is on main, align tree byte-identical. Gate: scalafmt both, align 143 JVM and 143 JS (was 138), fixtures 108, codec 95, compileAll, exit 0. bd-01M15ZMJC274ABA13QAMQ7XKYJ CLOSED.

M1 CHOSE A BETTER FIX THAN THE ONE I SPECIFIED, and the improvement is the point. I offered two options: exclude unranked and report it beside, or abstain above a stated threshold. It took the first and then made the pairing STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DOCUMENTARY. externalMass no longer returns a Double at all - it returns ExternalMassReport(attributed, unranked), and there is DELIBERATELY NO ACCESSOR FOR THE SUM. A caller cannot quote external mass without carrying the caveat, because the sum does not exist as a number anywhere in the API; anyone who genuinely wants it must write attributed + unranked at their own call site, where a reviewer can see them do it. rankedMass = 1 - unranked states the coverage of the attributed figure.

Its reasoning against my threshold option is correct and I should record it: a threshold needs a magic constant AND STILL HANDS BACK ONE NUMBER BELOW IT. This way there is no number to misquote at any threshold.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD. Design contract rule 8 says invalid states are unrepresentable. We have always applied that to DATA VALIDITY - smart constructors, phantom states, no forgeable receipts. m1 has just applied it to a REPORTING HAZARD: the danger was never that someone would compute the wrong sum, it was that someone would quote a correct sum as if it meant something it does not. Making the misleading number structurally unavailable is the same discipline aimed at a different failure. I want that generalised: WHERE A NUMBER IS ONLY HONEST WITH A CAVEAT ATTACHED, RETURN THE PAIR, NOT THE NUMBER AND A SCALADOC. A doc comment is advisory; a missing accessor is not.

And it did not renormalize the remaining five terms, per the estimand guard - the trap that would have traded one bias for its mirror.

Separately, both m1 and codex-storymodel4s-scout have just posted on the SAME risk - that three of us are about to fix one disease three different ways. That is exactly the concern behind my foundational-bead sequencing an hour ago, and I am ruling on it next.
